case_title: Atmaram S/O Raysingh Rathod v. State of Maharashtra
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to imprisonment of three years and a fine of Rs.5000/- each
high_court_outcome: Maintained conviction of the appellant and the sentence imposed upon him by the learned Sessions Judge
neutral_facts: The accused, his first wife, and his parents were prosecuted for offenses punishable under Sections 306 and 498A of the IPC on the allegations that the accused ill-treated the second wife of the accused and did not give her food for two days because she delivered a female child, as a result of which she jumped into a well with her daughter and committed suicide. The trial court convicted the accused of the offenses charged and sentenced them to imprisonment of three years and a fine of Rs.5000/- each. The High Court affirmed the conviction and sentence of the appellant, but acquitted the other accused. The prosecution relied on the evidence of the informant, the sister of the deceased, the Police Patil, and the Investigating Officer, as well as written undertakings signed by the accused and the deceased. The post mortem examination report described the deceased as 'well nourished' and indicated that she had her last meal within six hours, with no signs of severe beating. The accused's actions were alleged to have led to the deceased's suicide, but the court found that the prosecution failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the accused subjected the deceased to cruelty of the nature described in the Explanation to Section 498A, IPC.
